newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Shell discusses deadline with Nigeria's Ijaw.
newsitem.headline: Shell discusses deadline with Nigeria's Ijaw.

text.p: Nigeria's unit of Royal Dutch Shell Group said on Monday it was talking with four local communities in the midwest about a July 8 deadline to leave their oil-producing area or be forced out.
"We have opened dialogue with them officially," a Shell spokesman told Reuters in Lagos. "We believe we will be able to have a common ground."

In a letter to local newspapers last Wednesday, the ethnic Ijaw communities near Sokebelou in Delta State accused Shell of not providing local people with benefits from the 75,000 bpd of oil pumped into flow stations in the area.
"Shell must go if she does not change her shameless stand of disregard for the goose that lays the golden egg in this nation," their letter said.

The four communities recently won a battle against Shell in local courts over compensation of around 30 million naira ($350,000) for environmental damage, but a Shell spokesman said the company will appeal.
Shell says no compensation can be paid for the 1982 oil spill, from the trans-Forcados pipeline, because it was found to have been caused by sabotage. The company says it cleared up the spilled oil.

Ethnic clashes in March between Ijaw and Itsekiri tribesmen at nearby Warri forced Shell to close several oil wells earlier this year after fighting erupted over the relocation of a local government headquarters.

Shell came under fire from campaigners in 1995 after the execution for murder of author Ken Saro-Wiwa and eight other activists who campaigned for rights for the southeastern minority Ogoni community and against alleged pollution by Shell.
Shell pumps around half of Nigeria's roughly two million barrels per day oil production.
